reuse.why: The API and server consumers share getExpectedAmount and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but the existing getScheduledAmount retains a parallel amount-resolution path.

duplication.why: Range selection is shared, but getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount duplicate the missing, numeric and range dispatch.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization remaining in api-models.ts.

scope.why: The edits are focused on schedule amount planning, API exposure, associated tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Parallel amount helpers leave policy ownership ambiguous, while several comments and a release note still describe the superseded furthest-from-zero rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedAmount independently handles missing and numeric amounts instead of consolidating that dispatch with the existing getScheduledAmount abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedAmount reshapes getScheduledAmount's missing/numeric/range dispatch using early returns, leaving both implementations in place.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedAmount introduces the op parameter and isapprox branch, while getScheduledAmount independently resolves amounts through getRangeAmount rather than delegating to the complete expected-amount policy.
